results.title: TryTrustable: Compliance, security and AI governance on one control graph. | Product Hunt
results.content:
Title: TryTrustable: Compliance, security and AI governance on one control graph. | Product Hunt
## Compliance, security and AI governance on one control graph. One control, many regimes: logical access answers SOC 2 CC6.1, ISO 27001 A.8.2, GDPR Art. 32 and DPDP s.8(5) from a single result. Evidence is hash-chained as controls run — no screenshots, and exceptions are recorded as carefully as passes. Unusual: security testing (SAST, SCA, DAST, IaC, secrets) runs in your own CI rather than inferred from questionnaires. Consent sits on the same graph with a proof-of-consent ledger. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for TryTrustable. In most compliance tools you can mark a requirement complete and the readiness number goes up. So the number measures optimism, and you find out what was actually true during the audit. That is the thing we set out to remove. A statutory requirement maps to a shared control, a control maps to the checks that test it, and a check produces a dated result. Readiness is derived from the far end of that chain — there is no field to set it, every framework starts at zero, and a requirement with nothing behind it reads as "not modelled" rather than quietly counting as a pass. Because it is one control graph rather than eleven products, a failing check moves framework readiness, the residual score on the risk register and the attack-path graph in the same moment, instead of surfacing separately at the next audit. Answer logical access once and SOC 2 CC6.1, ISO 27001 A.8.2, GDPR Art. 32 and DPDP s.8(5) all read that one result. The security testing is real — SAST, SCA, DAST, IaC and secrets run inside your own pipeline rather than being inferred from cloud config and a questionnaire, and every integration is read-only. And consent management is part of the platform rather than something you buy elsewhere, with an append-only, hash-chained ledger proving what each person was shown, in which language, against which version of the notice. Worth saying plainly: SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certification are in progress, not complete. Happy to go deep on the control graph, the CI gate, the ledger design, or why the DPDP Act has no special category for sensitive personal data.
